current_status.to: Active, as amended. On 2026-05-19, City Council voted 7-2 to amend the moratorium to allow data centers using up to 75 megawatts of electricity to apply for zoning and construction permits, and carved out two named exemptions: the Scale Datacenters facility on the Expand Energy (formerly Chesapeake) campus (serving Cerebras AI), and the Rack59 Data Center at 7725 W. Reno Ave. As of the most recent reporting reviewed (dated 2026-06-25), no comprehensive data-center zoning use-unit had been adopted, so the underlying moratorium (through 2026-12-31 or earlier zoning adoption) remains in force. No source dated in July 2026 was located to independently confirm currency as of 2026-07-31.
current_status.reason: Confirmed via direct fetch of Oklahoma City Free Press reporting on the May 19, 2026 Council vote; no contrary evidence of full replacement or early termination was found.

evidence.title: City Council's data center exemptions raise questions of favoritism
evidence.supports: Oklahoma City Council voted 7-2 on 2026-05-19 to amend the data center moratorium to allow facilities up to 75 MW to apply for permits, with named exemptions for Scale Datacenters (Expand Energy campus) and Rack59 (7725 W. Reno Ave.).
evidence.quote: These are exemptions to the moratorium that we're creating. It does not exempt from the permitting or zoning that's required with this.

evidence.title: City Council puts hold on data centers to study electricity, water use
evidence.supports: Original moratorium adopted 2026-04-21, in effect through 2026-12-31 or until new regulations are codified.
evidence.quote: set to last until December 31st, 2026 or until new regulations for data centers are determined and codified by a new amendment or by the City's upcoming new Municipal Code

decisions.notes: No source dated in July 2026 discussing this moratorium was located; the most recent dated confirmation found (KGOU, 2026-06-25, news, not independently re-fetched in this pass) described the moratorium as still running through end of 2026 with the May 19 exceptions.
